messages.subject: Number of variables error
parts:
Hi,

I'm new to R and no statistics background, so I'm not sure if the code (based on code for Mathematica) is wrong or there is a bug in Renjin. 
The following works in Rstudio, but fails in Renjin with "org.renjin.eval.EvalException: number of variables != number of variable names"
Any idea what could be wrong?

Thanks! 

- J


xvals = c(-1.9137300, -0.9354530,  0.6309640,  0.3108570,  0.0431084)
yvals = c(-0.799904, -0.493735, -0.653075, -0.018258,  1.253210)
rvals = c(2.040010, 0.959304, 0.728477, 0.301885, 1.190120)

sample = data.frame(x=xvals, y=yvals, radius=rvals)
errors <- 1/sample$radius^2

print(sample)

fit <- nls(radius ~ sqrt(abs((x-x0))^2+abs((y-y0))^2), data = sample,
           start=list(x0=sample[1,]$x, y0=sample[1,]$y), weights = errors)

solution <- summary(fit)$coefficients[,1]
print(solution)
print(summary(fit))

messages.author: 2deb63de388ab75b
messages.subject: Re: Number of variables error
parts: It's this line that causes trouble in Renjin only, in RStudio it works:
fit <- nls(radius ~ sqrt(abs((x-x0))^2+abs((y-y0))^2), data = sample,
start=list(x0=sample[1,]$x, y0=sample[1,]$y), weights = errors)

I basically expect R to find me x0, y0, the approximate center of all the x,y values from the dataset, where each x,y value has a weight to indicate certain measurements that are less reliable. 
When I plot this result in Rstudio, it seems to give me a reasonably good answer, but this code could be wrong as well, it's my first time using R.

So does anyone have an idea where to look further, does my R code look right or could it be a problem with Renjin?

Thanks!

- J
